parts.label: (i)
parts.answer: $(3,1,-2)\cdot(1,1,2)=0$ and $(4,2,1)$ is not on $m$, so $l$ is parallel to $m$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Either: expand scalar product of a normal to $m$ and a direction vector of $l$. [M1]
Verify scalar product is zero. [A1]
Verify that one point of $l$ does not lie in the plane. [A1]
Or: substitute coordinates of a general point of $l$ into the equation of $m$ [M1]; obtain correct equation in $\lambda$ in any form [A1]; verify it is not satisfied for any $\lambda$ [A1]. Total 3.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Use correct method to evaluate a scalar product of normal vectors to $m$ and $n$. [M1]
Using the correct process for the moduli, divide the scalar product by the product of the moduli and evaluate the inverse cosine of the result. [M1]
Obtain $74.5^\circ$ or 1.30 radians. [A1] Total 3.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.answer: $7\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+7\mathbf k$ and $3\mathbf i+\mathbf j-\mathbf k$. The official MS prints the first vector as $7\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+7\mathbf j$; this is a printed anomaly, while $\lambda=3$ in the given line yields $7\mathbf k$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Either: using the components of a general point $P$ of $l$, form an equation in $\lambda$ by equating the perpendicular distance from $n$ to 2. [M1]
Or: take a point $Q$ on $l$, e.g. $(5,3,3)$, and form an equation in $\lambda$ by equating the length of the projection of $QP$ onto a normal to plane $n$ to 2. [M1]
Obtain a correct modular or non-modular equation in any form. [A1]
Solve for $\lambda$ and obtain a position vector for $P$, e.g. $7\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+7\mathbf j$ from $\lambda=3$. [A1] The official MS prints “$7\mathbf j$” as the third component; this is retained as a printed anomaly.
Obtain position vector of the second point, e.g. $3\mathbf i+\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ from $\lambda=-1$. [A1] Total 4.
